title: Power and Battery widget needs support for "multiple batteries for a single HID device"
line: Devices with several batteries, like earbuds with a case or split keyboards, now show each battery with its own number instead of the same name repeated.
explanation: Since UPower merged MR !337 (September 2026), each battery of a HID device with several batteries (Linux 7.1) reaches Plasma as its own UPower device, so the widget already lists all of them. But they all share the device's vendor and model, so the popup showed e.g. three identical "Sony WF-1000XM5" rows that couldn't be told apart. The battery model now appends "(Battery N)" when several batteries share a name, numbered in the natural order of their UPower paths (the kernel's battery report ids), and refreshes the names when batteries come and go.

commits.message:
components/batterycontrol: number batteries that share a device name

Devices like earbuds or split keyboards now show up with one battery per
part, but all of them got the same name, making them indistinguishable in
the Power and Battery widget. Each one now gets a "Battery N" suffix.

BUG: 518513

media.caption: A split keyboard (2 batteries) and earbuds (3 batteries): every battery shows the same device name
Each battery of the same device gets its own number
After one keyboard half disconnects, the remaining one goes back to the plain name

review.text: Clean, focused addition to BatteryControlModel that disambiguates multiple batteries sharing the same device name using natural numeric UDI sorting and a properly contextualized i18nc suffix, refreshing PrettyName on device add and removal. Given that Linux 7.1 HID multi-battery and UPower MR !337 do not expose semantic part labels (left/right/case), numbering by UDI order is the right Plasma-side UX and keeps labels stable across reconnects. Verified with realistic dbusmock multi-battery devices, hot-unplug back to the plain name, and passing batterycontroltest.

reviews.text: Clean, focused addition to BatteryControlModel that disambiguates multiple batteries sharing the same device name using natural numeric UDI sorting and a properly contextualized i18nc suffix, refreshing PrettyName on device add and removal. Given that Linux 7.1 HID multi-battery and UPower MR !337 do not expose semantic part labels (left/right/case), numbering by UDI order is the right Plasma-side UX and keeps labels stable across reconnects. Verified with realistic dbusmock multi-battery devices, hot-unplug back to the plain name, and passing batterycontroltest.

Now that UPower !337 is merged, numbering same-name batteries is a reasonable answer to the remaining KDE-side part of the wish, since the kernel and UPower give no per-part labels. The screenshots show it working for a split keyboard and earbuds. But the grouping key is only the display name, so two separate identical devices (two DualSense controllers, two identical mice) are now labelled "X (Battery 1)" and "X (Battery 2)", which wrongly says they are one device with two batteries. Per the reporter's c2, the batteries of one HID device share the UPower Serial, so that is the right key. The batterycontrol autotest, which already mocks UPower devices, also gets no coverage for the new naming.
changes: Group batteries by physical device as well as by name: read UPower's Serial property in UPowerBattery and number only batteries that share both name and serial (fall back to plain names when the serial is empty), so separate identical devices aren't presented as one multi-battery device

Add a case to components/batterycontrol/autotests/batterycontroltest.cpp: two batteries with the same vendor/model/serial get "(Battery 1)"/"(Battery 2)" in natural UDI order, the remaining one reverts to the plain name after removal, and two same-name devices with different serials keep plain names
